newsitem.title: USA: Clinton urges Congress act on trade, weapons.
newsitem.headline: Clinton urges Congress act on trade, weapons.

text.p: President Clinton on Friday urged Congress to act quickly to approve a treaty banning chemical weapons and to give him fast-track authority to negotiate a free-trade agreement with Chile.

In a speech to the American Society of Newspaper Editors, Clinton urged the Senate "to do what is right and ratify" the Chemical Weapons Convention, now bottled up in the Senate Foreign Relations Committee.

Clinton said that if the United States did not join nations that have already ratified the weapons treaty, it would be seen as a "rogue nation" like Iraq and Libya and its chemical companies would be subject to sanctions.

Clinton said he wanted to expand trade in Latin America at a time when many nations are turning more to European countries for trade. Fast-track authority would allow him to negotiate a treaty with Chile that Congress would have to vote for or against but would not be able to amend.
"If we don't seize these opportunities our competitors surely will," Clinton said.
Clinton said the United States faced a "moment of choice" and had to resist the temptation to remain inactive.
